description: src/lib.rs:56-69 + PLAN.md:70-89. The JmapChatExt trait + SessionClient wrapper is the deliberate orphan-rule-compliant pattern: we cannot implement methods directly on jmap_base_client::JmapClient (foreign type), so the trait + struct is the canonical Rust idiom. A future contributor reading the README might propose 'just add these methods to JmapClient via inherent impl' — that's an orphan-rule violation across crates and won't compile. The trait+wrapper isn't optional and isn't decorative; it's load-bearing. SessionClient also carries an owned Session per-call which is a deliberate cheap-clone choice (Session: Clone) rather than &Session lifetime gymnastics. Worth defending if a comment thread asks 'why isn't this just on JmapClient'.
title: DECISION: extension trait + SessionClient is the orphan-rule-compliant entry point
